entries.title: DRAFT: dependent covariance and variance in a log-concave posterior
entries.statement: DRAFT independent audit, pending w350 check. Let X=Exp(1)-1, s>0 and Z an independent N(0,1), Y=sX+sqrt(s)Z, A=Var(X|Y), and f(x)=x. Then X is isotropic log-concave in dimension one, E|Cov(f(X),X|Y)|^2=E A^2, and (E||Cov(X|Y)||_op)(E Var(f(X)|Y))=(E A)^2. Bayes' posterior is N((Y-1)/s,1/s) truncated below -1. Its variance is bounded, continuous and nonconstant, so E A^2>(E A)^2. Consequently the unweighted expectation-factorization shortcut is false in this class. This does not refute the variance-weighted bound or KLS.

entries.title: UNPROVED: uniform variance-weighted localization input
entries.statement: UNPROVED SUFFICIENT INPUT, not a theorem. There would exist universal T>0,K<infinity such that for every compactly supported full-dimensional isotropic log-concave mu in every R^n, X~mu independent of Brownian B, mu_t=Law(X|Y_r:0<=r<=t), Y_t=tX+B_t, every smooth fixed f, and a.e. 0<t<T, E|Cov_mu_t(f,X)|^2 <= K E Var_mu_t(f). The same constants must work for all dimensions, measures and functions. Unweighted covariance expectation bounds do not establish this input.
assumptions: universal quantifiers over f and mu

entries.title: DRAFT: Poincare reduction conditional on a weighted input
entries.statement: DRAFT conditional reduction, pending referee check. For compactly supported isotropic log-concave mu and Brownian observation mu_t, assume E|Cov_mu_t(f,X)|^2<=K E Var_mu_t(f) for every smooth f and a.e. 0<t<T. Also use the T-strong-convexity posterior inequality C_P(mu_T)<=1/T. Innovation Ito isometry gives V_f'(t)=-E|Cov_mu_t(f,X)|^2, where V_f(t)=E Var_mu_t(f). Gronwall and E mu_T|grad f|^2=mu|grad f|^2 then give C_P(mu)<=exp(KT)/T. The universal weighted hypothesis is unproved here; this is not a KLS proof.
assumptions: the uniform variance-weighted estimate is assumed

entries.title: DRAFT: fourth moments do not guarantee exponential tilt derivatives
entries.statement: DRAFT scope correction, pending independent check. Let R have density 5r^(-6) on r>=1, S an independent fair sign, and X=sqrt(3/5)SR. Then E X=0, E X^2=1 and E X^4=9/5, but E exp(zX)=infinity for every real z!=0. Thus isotropy and finite fourth moments alone do not define an exponential tilt average near zero. Require finite Laplace transform on a neighborhood, or define f -> (1/2)E[f(XX^T-I)] algebraically and identify it with a tilt derivative only when tilts exist. This counterexample is not log-concave and does not refute the log-concave target.
assumptions: scope is general probability laws with finite fourth moments

entries.title: DRAFT: equality witness for partial tensor symmetrization
entries.statement: DRAFT independently derived equality witness, pending w350 check. Let 1<=p<=q, dim H>=2, P_q average permutations of the first q positions in H^(tensor(p+q)), and choose orthonormal binary basis e0,e1. For each coordinate let a be the number of ones in its first p positions. Set T=(-1)^a/binom(q,p-a) if the total number of ones is p, and 0 otherwise. T is separately symmetric in its first p and last q positions. A finite-difference identity gives P_qT=(-1)^p block_swap(T)/binom(q,p), so ||T||/||P_qT||=binom(q,p). Tensoring with a nonzero vector in any auxiliary Hilbert space preserves equality. This witness alone is not an upper-bound proof or a KLS proof.

relations.rationale: The reduction assumes this universal weighted estimate and does not derive it.
The counterexample explains why the weighted input cannot be replaced by a product of unweighted expectations.
The exact counterexample rules out a shortcut in a localization route to the same isotropic log-concave Poincare/Cheeger problem.
If its universal input is proved, this conditional variance-retention reduction yields the target Poincare bound.
The witness checks sharpness of the deterministic tensor-recovery component in the tilt-derivative route; no universal analytic input is supplied.
